utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. May I remind you, sir, that the affirmation you made still applies. Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, and good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Ostreni.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you remember, Mr. Ostreni, on Friday, when we left off, I was asking you a question about an incident that took place near the village of Vejce on the 28th of April, 2001? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall asking me -- asking you whether you could recall a number of condemnations, in particular by the US administration, in relation to this incident? Do you recall those questions?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you asked me about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'd like to show you a document, Mr. Ostreni.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It is Rule 65 ter 1D956, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Ostreni, the document that will appear on your screen is a press statement issued by the deputy spokesman of the United States Department of State, State Department, and it's dated the 28th of April of 2001. I will read the relevant passage to you. It says this: "The United States condemns the attack by armed ethnic Albanian extremists today on Macedonia security forces, which resulted in the death of eight Macedonian soldiers. We extend our condolences to the families of those that were killed. "The United States calls upon all political parties and groups in Macedonia to join in condemning the senseless act of violence and to continue the process of political dialogue in which they are engaged." Mr. Ostreni, my question is this: Do you recall having received information to the effect that this attack in Vejce had been condemned in those terms by the US State Department?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, we followed, to the extent we could, what was going on, on the political scene; but I believe that it is important to describe the situation in general, in which this territory found itself at that time. I'm not denying that the United States said what they said, as you're putting it, but it is important to explain that this happened in the combat area of 112 Brigade, and after the MX operation, when the police forces started to vandalize and terrorise the population in that area. Unfortunately, on the 2nd of April, a 16-year-old young man was killed. He was from the village of Selci. He was killed by the police forces. As for this vandalism that I mentioned, I would call on Fakti newspaper of 5th April where a statement was issued and concerns were raised regarding the situation with the Albanians living in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: So the units of that brigade then had a clash with the units of the Macedonian army and; as a consequence of that, what happened, happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ostreni. I'll ask you if, it you can to try to respond to the question as shortly as you can; and if you feel have you to explain it further, by all means. There's another document that I would like to show you, Mr. Ostreni, in relation to this matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It's Exhibit 1D231.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Ostreni, this is a transcript of a press briefing. It is, again, from the same origin. It comes from the State Department of the United States of America, and this one is dated the 30th of April of 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'd ask the registry to go to page 1D00-78 -- 7189, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Ostreni, this is a part of the press briefing of the State Department, which is devoted to the situation in Macedonia, and the department spokesman of the State Department is being asked questions about the incident in Vejce. He said this: "We did issue a statement on Saturday, soundly condemning the attack on Macedonian security forces by armed ethnic Albanian extremists, and that statement obviously still stands."

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It's a bit further down the page, please. Thank you. It start with the word: "Well, I will just point ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The spokesman, Mr. Ostreni, goes on to say this: "This was an ambush by extremists that resulted in the death of eight Macedonian soldiers. We want to extend our condolences to the families of those eight who were killed and the entire country of Macedonia." Then, in the next paragraph, the spokesman of the State Department says this: "We noted or have discussed that there has been a strong condemnation of that barbarous attack by the Macedonian Albanian political leader, Arben Xhaferi." We have encouraged other ethnic Albanian leaders to condemn this extremist violence, as well." And, then, in the next paragraph, he says this: "We very much support the necessary steps Macedonia is taking to prevent armed extremists from disrupting interethnic cooperation and dialogue which has been taking place in Macedonia over the last few weeks. I think it should be said that such violence and terrorist activity greatly harms the interests of the ethnic Albanians in Macedonia and throughout the region, and those that are perpetrating this type of violence should realise it." My question is again, Mr. Ostreni, the same: Were you aware of the condemnations in the terms that I have read out to you, barbarous attack, extremist violence, and terrorist activity, which were used at the time to condemn the attack in Vejce? Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The text you just read was interpreted to me into Albanian. I don't know if it is the way you're putting it, because it is not written in a language that I understand; but, however, I will trust you and I will answer you the following: We were, at that time, acting exclusively against the police and military forces of the Republic of Macedonia. We were in a war situation, and that's why our clashes with the armed forces of the government of the Republic of Macedonia at that time were called by our population as just and as clashes directed at creating the conditions for changing the constitution and for securing all rights for the Albanians, as mentioned in communique number 6 and in the memorandum. So I'm not denying that this could have been said by the United States of America, but I cannot claim this with full certainty because I cannot follow the text in English as I would if it were in Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful for that, Mr. Ostreni. But the clarification I'm seeking from you is whether at the time, in the year 2001, and more specifically in the month of April or May of 2001, you were aware of these condemnations of your attack by the US government.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, we were following what the US ambassador to the Republic of Macedonia was saying, what the ambassador of the United Kingdom to the Republic of Macedonia was saying, amongst others. He, in a way, explained the constitution of the Republic as a source of the clashes between the Albanians and the government. He said, in a diplomatic way - but this is how I understood it - due to the preamble, that excluded the Albanians and defined the state only as one nation state of the Macedonian, ethnic Macedonians; and amongst other things, he said that he would have been offended had he been an Albanian living in the Republic of Macedonia. So there are many changes, transformation of views, on the situation in Macedonia before these events. It was promoted as an oasis of peace, in the decision making centres in the US, in NATO, and the European Union, and so on. I apologise, but I would like to add that at that time congressmen from the state, four of them, addressed the president of the Republic of Macedonia through a letter, asking and demanding that the rights of the Albanians were secured. What you calling negative, as far as the activities of Albanians are concerned, there are many articles published in Albanian newspapers saying that the Albanians should get their elementary rights and freedoms.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, thank you for that, Mr. Ostreni. I think you still haven't answered the question; and, simply, as a matter of clarification, did you or did you not -- were you or were you not aware, in late April or early May of 2001, of the condemnations by the US government of your attack - and let's keep it at that at this point - in Vejce? Were you aware of this? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. Of course, there were -- there was a great flow of information at that time. Maybe I was aware. But since the six years have passed, it is difficult for me to remember all the details regarding issues that you are questioning me about.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And can you recall perhaps that two days after the attack by your organisation in Vejce, your organisation was listed by the State Department in a document called, Patterns of Global Terrorism, where you were being condemned for not only attacking government forces, as it says, but for "harassing and detaining civilians and indiscriminately firing at civilian centres." Do you recall this document or the fact that you were so listed?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know which document you're referring to. Maybe you should give me the title of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I will show it to you, Mr. Ostreni.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: This is Rule 65 ter 1D887, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Ostreni, this is the excerpt of a document which come from the US Department of State. It is called, Patterns of Global Terrorism. It's dated April the 30th, 2001, and it's released by the office of the coordinator for counterterrorism. I will read to you the section of document which is relevant here.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If the registry could scroll down, very much. It starts with the word, "In south-eastern Europe." I will read it out to you. It says this: "In south-eastern Europe, groups of ethnic Albanians have conducted armed attacks against government forces in southern Serbia and in Macedonia since 1999. One group in southern Serbia called itself the Liberation Army of Presevo, Medvedja, and Bujanovac. One group in Macedonia calls itself the National Liberation Army, NLA. "Both groups include members who fought to with the Kosovo Liberation Army in 1998/1999, and have used their wartime connections to obtain funding and weapons from Kosovo and elsewhere. The PMBLA has, on occasion, harassed and detained civilians travelling through areas it controls. Both the PMBLA and the NLA have fired indiscriminately upon civilian centres. "In the same region, ethnic Albanian assailants carried out a terrorist attack against a bus in Kosovo on 16 February 2001, killing at least seven civilians and wounding 43 others." Before I ask you this, Mr. Ostreni, there was a similar document in 2002 which related to the period of 2001. My question is: Are you aware of these documents or the fact that you were so listed by the State Department in those terms?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not aware. For me, it is important that the National Liberation Army was not on the list of terrorist organisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, let me just wrap things up briefly with regard to the Vejce incident. I'll ask whether you are aware that the Presidency of the EU called your attack in Vejce a vicious attack. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not, but they did not call it a terrorist attack. It was part of the war. The war is ugly because people lose their lives, but these people were armed, uniformed, and they were tasked to fight against the forces of the National Liberation Army. This would be my answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And so the answer is, No, you were not aware of the EU condemnation in terms of vicious attack. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember being aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you recall NATO calling this attack a cowardly act of extremists. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you recall France calling the attack a terrorist act?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall that. I wasn't able to follow everything that you mention. I had work to do on a daily basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you recall the EU Commissioner for External relations, Chris Patten at the time, calling it a senseless act of murder? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And are you aware of the fact, Mr. Ostreni, that the murders in Vejce are one of the basis upon which the Macedonian authorities had investigated the leadership of your organisation, including yourself? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not informed. I didn't receive any document. I know that the Macedonian authorities have not issued any indictment or pressed any charges against the person who killed the 16-year-old and against those who terrorised the population in that part. They -- their stance was anti-Albanian, and they would only inform of cases alleged that were committed by the National Liberation Army. As I mentioned, there were other cases where the perpetrators were the other side, as a case of killing the pizzeria and the above mentioned case.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you are not aware that the incident in Vejce is one of the cases that were sent by the local prosecutor to the Prosecutor of this Tribunal for investigation. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I have a general proposition for you, Mr. Ostreni. Would you agree that if the crimes that I've described to last week and briefly this morning have, in fact, that been committed as they have been put to you, this would suggest that the orders which you said you gave or, more specifically, Mr. Ahmeti, you said, gave to respect humanitarian law and not to commit any crimes would have been disregarded? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't agree with that, because these are clashes between the NLA, its members, and the members of the armed forces of the army and the police. This did not start on the 28th of April but much earlier, in February, and it was ongoing. The operation in Tetovo was carried out on the 25th and continued through to 26th; then, the MX operation, MX-1, takes hold on the 28th in Kumanova, and this was within that ongoing war between the armed forces of the Republic of Macedonia and the NLA. There was no individual case here, but it was part of the ongoing war.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So your evidence, Mr. Ostreni, is that at no time during the crisis in 2001 did you become aware of any crime having been committed by any member of your organisation. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. I was not aware if it happened the way you're putting it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you another question, Mr. Ostreni. You've -- do you remember indicating to the Office of the Prosecutor that you had requested -- you or Mr. Ahmeti had requested the so-called brigades to keep lists of personnel or members which then should be submitted to the Main Staff? Do you recall saying them that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recall, but by leave of Their Honours, I would like to explain something. Honoured counsel, from the very beginning, you are referring to the NLA as the so-called NLA. Now you also refer to the brigades as the so-called brigades. I would like to point out that the competent organs in the Republic of Macedonia did not use this term. Just to inform the Trial Chamber and yourself, Mr. Counsel, after the war, the Association of War Veterans of the NLA was established. This association was registered on the 5th of May 2002 at the Tetovo Court; and later on, it was adopted by the constitutional court. So these are the brigades of the NLA and the NLA, and not the brigades of the so-called NLA, as you're referring to it. So the competent authorities adopted this term by the mere fact that the Association of War Veterans of the NLA was created and registered at the Tetovo Court.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'll grateful for that, Mr. Ostreni, and I'll repeat the question: Were you -- or is it correct that you or Mr. Ahmeti had issued an order that the so-called brigades of your organisation should keep lists of personnel or members that they should provide to the Main Staff. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't issue such an order, and was not entitled to give such orders. I organised things so that the administration and records are well organised and all documents collected in the General Staff. However, this did not happen, and the documents remained at the brigade levels.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I will read to you a short passenger, a short statement that you made to the Office of the Prosecutor during proofing. You said this: "After the Ohrid Agreement, the commander of the brigades should have kept the records and submitted them to the General Staff. However, the brigade commander didn't do it, as far as I know, with the exception of the 116, as the conditions were not adequate. I think I sent the brigade commanders an order to submit the records to the General Staff." Do you recall telling that to the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember. I didn't say records, but I said we must prepare the archives, to hand it over to the General Staff. In the case of Brigade 116, the commander passed by and handed over them.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: An aside from the commander of that brigade, the others didn't provide those documents to the so-called Main Staff. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. The documents remained there because we were busy handing over the weapons and taking care of all the documents related to it. So they remained at brigade levels.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall that you also indicated, both to my colleague from the Prosecution and also in one of the documents that was shown to you, that the individuals who were to join your organisation should take a military oath, which you said was an important part of your organisation? And my question is: Did you ever verify whether people joining your organisation were, in fact, taking such oath at the time of joining?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see it personally, because they were obliged to act in that way. When voluntaries came and reported to brigades, there was a small training centre where they took the oath, and I believe they did do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So just to clarify this, you did not verify whether the order, which was given in that regard, was, in fact, complied with. You simply believe it was. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time that I worked, the NLA front extended to over 200 kilometres. It was impossible for me because I had to leave my post, to see how things were developing on the ground. Therefore, I could only talk with people on the phone, get information from them, and talk with people who passed by the General Staff who informed us of the situation, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that would be the same, Mr. Ostreni, in regard to training, which you said had to take place with new recruits. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The training at the NLA was a specific one. Part of it took place in the training centre of the brigades, then the person was included in the reservists of the brigade. Gradually, then they were transferred to the first front line, and then other brigades were formed. So the soldier wasn't sent immediately to the front line, because he wasn't trained for that, hadn't done the military service. So our training was, how to say, small-scale training, simple training. It didn't have the necessary expertise and equipment to train them. So they learned as they were fighting and participating in the events this will you this became good fighter. Then from Brigade 112 was formed 115 Brigade, which as for Radusa; from 112 Brigade, 116 Brigade was formed; from 113 Brigade, 114 was formed, and so on. I tried, as our possibilities were, to prevent the newly joined soldiers to be sent immediately to the front line, but let them get used to developments for a while and then send them to the front. This is how training was done. So first he was acquainted with the weapon, taught how to line up, how to wear the uniform, how to --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... the question was much narrower in scope. The question was about you and whether you were being able to ensure that the order, which you had given that training should take place, was actually enforced with all new recruits. My question is: Were you able to do so; or, as in the case, of the military oath, you simply assumed that your orders were being followed?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had proof of that, because Mr. Ali Ahmeti toured the brigades, followed up the situation. There was a training centre in Brodec, in the meadows there,. When I saw there myself later, I saw what was going on. So all the brigades had received instructions to train new recruits, to give them the elementary train.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct that you told the Office of the Prosecutor that your organisation had a military-like sort of discipline? Do you recall saying that, or something to that effect?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall that. We always tried to apply military discipline, in order for us to keep the situation under control, the NLA units along with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Did you have any courtrooms in the NLA, Mr. Ostreni?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We couldn't have a courtroom, because we didn't have the laws to try people. We didn't have the persons trained to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you have judges or prosecutors in the NLA?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We had ordinary soldiers who might have graduated for law, but not judges and prosecutors as such.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Ant is it correct that, although you had a group that was referred to as a military police, it actually never functioned at the military -- as a military police and did not perform any specific tasks that military police would normally perform? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is true. From the war experience in Kosova, they tried to form that unit called military police; but the way we organised the formation, they became part of the units.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you explained, I think, to my colleague that there wasn't really a need for any structure or institutionalisation of disciplinary matters, since you said were not informed of any breach of discipline in the NLA in the year 2001. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct that I was not directly informed by the brigades. It is correct that our rules were provided disciplinary measures to be taken by the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, let's turn to a different topic, Mr. Ostreni, which is the issue of the strategy and method which were used by your organisation during this year. Is it correct that understand that you told the Office of the Prosecutor that the method and strategies which you and other members of the organisation used were those of a regular military organisation? Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is my evidence; namely, that we tried, as much as we could, to attain the level of regular military discipline.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'm putting to you something quite different, Mr. Ostreni, and I will ask you whether you agree or disagree with me. I'm putting to you that the strategy of your organisation consisted in attacking soft or easier targets, such as police stations or convoy, with a view to trigger a disproportionate reaction on the part of the authority that would you in turn use for propaganda purposes to increase the support of your organisation. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will hear what you are going to put to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, can you first, perhaps, simply answer whether you agree or disagree with that proposition.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The fighting was regulated or is regulated everywhere by rules, and we used the most suitable rules given the level of the NLA. Finally, on the 1st of May, Units 113 came out in well known positions, and then we come to the stage of the different use of force. We haven't used anything that is not foreseen in military rules.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is it correct that your strategy, all through the year 2001, Mr. Ostreni, was, in fact, and almost exclusively to attack soft targets in hit-and-run fashion, to trigger a disproportionate reaction by the Macedonian authorities, with a view to use this overreaction for propaganda purposes? Do you agree that was your strategy?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is not true. It may have happened somewhere incidently; but, in general, we have operated through obvious actions on front line. More, we have been involved in an active defence, rather than retreats or such hit-and-run attacks, as you say. As I am saying, we have been engaged more in an active defence because we believed that it was the best tactic at the time of the development of the brigades, since we were supposed to be engaged in a general military operation afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And as far as methods are concerned, methods which were used by your organisation in 2001, do you agree that they consisted almost exclusively in the commission of crimes and terrorist actions, with a view to force the authorities and the international community to negotiate with you? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not agree with this. There was an internal strive in Macedonia between the Albanians and the government. This army was introduced as a National Liberation Army. This was done because of the violation of the rights and freedoms of Albanians and the demonstration of force by the Macedonian government prior to 1991; and, especially more so after 1991, with intervention and demonstration of police force in a village off Struke called Ladoliste [phoen]; then in Bit Pazar; then the destruction of the university building in Tetovo, founded and financed by the Albanian population; then prevention of development in the pedagogical faculty; and, finally, the brutal acts by the police in Gostivar.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Mr. Ostreni, let's stick with 2001; and at this stage, I'm asking you -- I'll ask you the question a bit differently, if that helps. Do you agree that the commission of crimes or terrorist attacks by members of your organisation was not just an accident but that it was, in fact, the method chosen by your organisation to conduct your activities against the Macedonian state? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not agree with that. We didn't act on an individual basis. People were involved in units, and the goal was not a terrorist attack but an uprising carried out through this NLA, which was in the phase of development, and had to confront the forces of the government of the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can the witness please be shown what is Exhibit 1D227, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Ostreni, this is an article called: "Will Macedonia be next?" This comes from a military review called Jane's Intelligence Digest, and it is dated the 2nd of February of 2001. I'd like to read a passage to from the last page of that article.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That's 1D00-6055. The paragraph starts with the words, "At present." That's the second paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The magazine, Mr. Ostreni, said the following: "At present, KLA terrorism in Macedonia is still a relatively minor issue, just as it was in Kosovo from 1995 to 1998. The KLA started its activities by attacking Serbian police patrols. However, the ultimate aim is to provoke the authorities into making a military response which will serve to unite the ethnic Albanian minority in western Macedonia." Mr. Ostreni, do you agree with this analysis of Jane's Digest, to the effect that the aim of those hit-and-run attacks that your organisation was organised at the time was to trigger a disproportionate military response by the Macedonian authorities? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not agree with that. I do not, because our brigades developed from smaller groups into squads, platoons, battalions, and so on, and we tried not to organise hit-and-run attacks, but, as I said, an active defence in order to defend ourselves in case of attacks and gradually expand the territory under our control by increasing the number of your units with new volunteers.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Let's see another evaluation then, this time from the month of May 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: This is Exhibit 1D232, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Ostreni, the documents that I'm about to show you is a compilation, if you wish, of reports or press reports by an organisation called the Balkan Human Rights. It is prepared, I believe, by the Euro-Balkan Institute.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I would ask the registry to turn to third page of that document, which is 1D00-6272. If it could be scrolled down a little bit, and a bit more, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Ostreni, there is a section of that document which starts with the title, "Rebels are causing civilian casualties," and I would like to read it to you. It says this: "A senior NATO officially claimed that the rebels were trying to lure the Macedonian army into causing civilian casualties that they could then exploit for propaganda purposes." And then there is a quote, which says: "Let's face it," said the senior western European NATO officer. And there is a quote again: "KLA saw what the results were when the Serbs killed 45 Kosovars at Racak, and they are thinking of the propaganda value of something like that being made to happen in Macedonia." Then the text goes on to say: "Other NATO officials and Macedonian defence sources fear that the thousands of civilians trapped against their will in villages under constant bombardment north of Tetovo, just ten miles from Kosovo border, are being held by NLA rebels partly as 'human shields' and partly because the Macedonian forces would be almost certain to kill civilians if they launch a ground assaulted." Mr. Ostreni, focussing perhaps more specifically on Kumanovo, were you aware at all that members of your organisation would actually use or keep civilians for the purpose of using the eventual or possibly death or injury for propaganda purposes? Is that information which you had in your possession at the time?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was a media war waged in all the media outlets of the Republic of Macedonia, where the government brought constant pressure to prove that the NLA members are using the civilian population as human shield. At that time I, too, stated that they should go and talk directly to the population and find out for themselves what they think about the situation, because the citizens there, women, children, elderly people, had their sons, fathers, or brothers, husbands, in the ranks of the NLA that was operating in that area. It is not possible, theoretically or practically speaking, that someone who has at home the wife, mother, sister, children, or father, to use them as human shields and protect himself by so doing. I said then, and I'm saying now, that the war in the Republic of Macedonia was waged for the -- for the protection or for winning human rights and freedoms of the people. What sense would it have if we killed children, women, elderly people, and then enjoyed our rights and freedoms at that expense? Third, if the NLA committed such an act, it would certainly not have the support of the Albanian population, as it did almost 100 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Apparently, you have more information from Macedonian language newspapers. If you look at the Albanian language newspapers, you will see there statements issued by chairman of municipalities who worked and lived in that area, and none of them had declared that the NLA has used them as human shields and forced them to remain there. In a television programme --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... just stay with me for a second. The question is about the strategy of the NLA, and my question is a simple one. Do you agree or disagree with the proposition that the strategy of your organisation was to provoke a repressive military response by the Macedonian authorities? Do you agree or not?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree with the fact that the NLA and its strategy was to pressure the government of the Republic of Macedonia, to reconcile with the granting of the freedoms and rights to the Albanian citizens in this republic, beginning with the amendment of the preamble to the constitution, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So, in answer to my question, you do not agree with the proposition that the strategy of your organisation was to provoke a repressive military response and to gain support from that response from the population? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There are a number of communiques that the Prosecution submitted here, whereby we demand that the war come to an end and give priority to dialogue to the solution of the crisis.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can the witness please be shown what is Exhibit 1D228, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Ostreni, do you know who Ambassador Pardew is?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree that that Mr. or Ambassador Pardew was involved during the crisis period with the negotiation of the, among other things, the Ohrid Framework Agreement? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, Mr. Ostreni, just looking at the document in front of you, there is a passage that I want to show you, to familiarise yourself with this. This is a record of a hearing before the Committee on Foreign Relations of the United States Senate, and it relates to the crisis in Macedonia, in particular, and it is dated the 13 June 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I would like to the registry to please turn to page 1D00-6292.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Ostreni, Ambassador Pardew appeared before the Senate committee on that occasion and, he was asked a number of questions pertaining to the crisis in Macedonia. One of the question that he was asked was about the strategy of your or the ways of your organisation, and he said this.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: This is the second full paragraph on that page, and it starts with the word: "Its strategy."

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Pardew said this: "Its strategy is the same strategy that we encountered in Serbia; that is, to provoke a repressive military and to gain support from that response from the population." So, in view of your response, Mr. Ostreni, before, I suppose you will disagree with the assessment of Ambassador Pardew, that it was your strategy to provoke repressive military response and to gain support for that response from the population. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Our strategy was to bring pressure to bear on the government to sit down with us and make political changes or amendments to the constitution and other laws, in order to provide Albanians with their human rights and freedoms. Albanians, who were exempted from power when Macedonia, had officially declared that it was a state of only of the Macedonians. We have lived there. We live there, and we will live there. Therefore, we wish to be part of the government and have the right, equal rights, with the Macedonian citizens there.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But do you agree, Mr. Ostreni, that at all stages in 2001, from the beginning of the year to the end of the year, there were several ethnic Albanians who were members of the government? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, in the Balkans, in the former Yugoslavia, it was a tradition that the chairman of the Presidency of Yugoslavia be one of them be Albanian. There were Albanians in position. There were also some Albanians who had official positions in Macedonia, but it doesn't mean that Albanians, in general, enjoy their rights and freedoms. This fact cannot be taken as a fact to prove that Albanians had these rights and freedoms. When there were Albanians, we had, for example, 180 policemen who were Albanians out of 10.000 policemen. We were very little represented in all areas. Our language was not an official language. Our rights to using our national symbols were restricted. Our education, we could only have two per cent of Albanians attending universities. In the academy of science, there wasn't any member who was Albanian. So that was a policy that wanted to show to Europe and the world, just as it did during the time when Yugoslavia was in place, to show as if Albanians are in leadership, when in reality the population, in general, were not duly represented to all the government associations and institutions.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But, surely, you will agree, Mr. Ostreni, that as of the middle of May 2001, all major political parties that represented the interests of the Albanian community were, in fact, part of the government. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree that an extended coalition government was formed, part of which were also political parties, with which the NLA had assigned the Prizren agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you didn't stop your attacks on civilian population and state authorities after the grand coalition was formed. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, we were being attacked. On the 25th of May, there was a powerful operation in Vaksince launched, and I have the impression that this is an agreement with the accord of Pande Petreski and the Serb general who had who intervene with their forces to restore the five kilometre border belt controlled by the NATO forces. At that time, on the 25th of May, they wanted to celebrate Tito's birthday, and they undertook this Vaksince operation which ensued in severe fighting. So it was not -- we were not in a position to stop it. They were a larger force than us. They had to stop their operation and start negotiations for realising the demands of the Albanians. I have the impression, however, that at that time the government, unfortunately, at a parliamentary session, where the extended coalition government was formed, in one of the three or four points, it aimed at the abolition on the NLA, but it was termed in other terms. So, at the time, for us, it was impossible, as I said, to undertake an operation. On the contrary, we were the ones who were attacked.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Ms. Regue is on her feet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I was simply going to point out that my colleague, within the question, he put at the time same level the attacks against civilian population and attacks against the state authorities. So I believe that should have been distinguished from putting the questions, because we are talking about two issues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm not sure that that troubled the answer at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Ostreni, let's go back, then, to the issue of strategy, what you say was the strategy of your organisation, and I'd lake to show you yet another document about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: This is Exhibit P485, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Ostreni, this is - or this will be, in any case - a document that was prepared by the military security service of the army of the Republic of Macedonia. It was provided to us by the Office of the Prosecutor, and I would like to show what you is at page 1D00-9148. This is a part, Mr. Ostreni, as you will see that discusses various aspects of the NLA, its strategy, its capabilities, and its weaknesses. I will go through those with you. I think there is a Macedonian version on the ride of your screen, Mr. Ostreni, if that assists. First, I will read to you what this document says about the strategy of your organisation. It says this: "To attract and to maintain international attention and intervention, partition and dissemination of the army of the Republic of Macedonia, abuse of the oversensitivity of Slavs to guerilla warfare, engagement of NATO, and maintaining of the engagement; and, secondly, to take over control of the undefended territory and protection of the same with minimum losses to avoid close combat, to force the government of the Republic of Macedonia to negotiate." Mr. Ostreni, do you think that this is a pretty fair assessment of the strategy of your organisation in the year 2001?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to read it in myself. Once again, could you please point out the paragraph. Is it the subtitle: The NLA strategy?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. That would be the first highlighted subheading in the Macedonian version, which is at the top of your screen.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an attempt to carry out an analysis. It is quite normal for the NLA to try and attract the attention of the government in order to try and negotiations. At the same time, it sought the engagement of NATO and international decision making centres, in order to facilitate a solution to the problems in Macedonia. The same, more or less, was stated by the International Crisis Group, in a document published on 9th of April. This was published at the time in Flaka and Fakti newspapers.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But is it correct, Mr. Ostreni, that your way to attract attention in 2001 was by committing crimes or terrorist acts or by trying to trigger an overreaction by the Macedonian authorities? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Honourable counsel, by committing crimes or other acts, as you describe them, you cannot attract the international community and make them assist you. You would achieve the opposite effect. That's why we were very careful not to commit any acts that would resemble terrorist acts. Our main goal was to be open and to be very clear and precise on what our demands were as a National Liberation Army, so that the international community was clear, too, on our demands. That's why, in our communique number 6, in our memorandum, as well as in other communiques, we regularly sought international assistance in resolving this issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Isn't the truth, Mr. Ostreni, that what you sought to achieve was to create fear in the population and thus pressure the government to negotiate with you? I'll going to ask you with perhaps one example: Are you aware of a commander from your organisation, a man known as Hoxha, threatening to bomb Skopje? Are you aware of those threats?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In a very difficult psychological situation, it is true that Hoxha issued such a statement. But immediately afterwards, Hoxha in his statement said that he would carry out that thing in order -- if he received an order from the General Staff of the National Liberation Army. That's why the journalists asked me that what the order of the General Staff would be at that time. I told the journalist that it would be the just order. So, in other words, nothing would happen and equipments would not be used. It is questionable whether Hoxha had that or not, but that's what he stated. But my reply was that the order of the General Staff would be just, an order that would be in compliance with the norms and law, and that would avoid any damage caused to Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you aware of similar threats being made by a man called Dren Korabi? Are you aware of any threats, public threats, being made by this person?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please define this "threat" that he made.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, were you aware, for instance, that Mr. Korabi had suggested that civilians should be expelled from certain areas? Is that something that you are aware of?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was not aware of this, and I really don't believe that Dreni stated something like this. But to answer your question, I was not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you aware, perhaps, that members of your organisations on a number of occasions tried to kill civilians-- I'm sorry, politicians, ministers, for instance, that were in the government in Macedonia at that time?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In which time-period, please? Is it the same time-period from 16th of February up to the mobilisation of the NLA, or is it outside this time-frame?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you aware, for instance, of an attack on the convoy of the Minister of the Interior at the time, Mr. Boskoski, on 29th or 30th of July, in the area near Lavce [phoen]? Are you aware of this attack?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you aware, perhaps, of an attack in the month of March 2001, again against the convoy of Mr. Boskoski, which also carried the deputy Minister of the Interior, an Albanian called Refet Elmazi? Are you aware that your organisation, or members thereof, attacked this convoy? Perhaps to assist you, it was in the location called Brest.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that there were complications at Brest at that time because the persons in question were sent there to establish police stations, and those who undertook that operation did not find that idea very suitable.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But you must be aware, however, Mr. Ostreni, that the attack, in fact, took place and that the convoy was attacked. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And going back for a minute to Exhibit P485, I would like to show another part of that document to Mr. Ostreni. This would be the second header on that same page in the Macedonian version, and it reads: "NLA capabilities." For the English version, this would be towards the bottom of the page. If the registry could scroll down a little bit more, thank you, and enlarge, perhaps, the bottom paragraph. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Ostreni, I will read it out to you. The document say this is about the NLA capabilities: "First ambush, attack on weak targets (patrols that wander off, lightly armed soldiers, and police); breakthrough (attack) (attack on significant infrastructure targets) special activities units; diversion and sabotage (attacks on positions of the army of Republic of Macedonia/Ministry of Internal Affairs, with light weapons and disturbing fire); mining (the use of anti-tank and anti-personnel mines with hidden fire), (protection of lateral sides)." Do you agree, Mr. Ostreni, that at the time, in 2001, those were some of the capabilities - we will call them that - that were used and employed by your organisation to carry out its attacks?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not all of them. You are asking me for a series of activities. You can ask me one by one, and then I will give you my reply. But as you are putting it, all collectively for sabotage activities, mine planting, that was not our capability.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, I'll put, in particular perhaps, the last one to you. Is it correct or do you recall telling this to the Prosecution: "We did not have anti-tank mines. I sent my instructions not to use mines, because it is prohibited also by international law. However, I cannot exclude the possibility that some units had them." Do you recall that this is in your statement -- or the proofing note, I apologise, -- in the statement to the Office of the Prosecutor? Do you recall telling them that as far as you knew, the NLA did not have any tank mines or didn't use any such thing, do you recall that, or mines?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is it your evidence that at no time, during the crisis in 2001 up to the Ohrid Framework Agreement, you did not become aware of the fact that your organisation possessed mines and actually used them? Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was made aware only when, without our authorisation, in the 116th Brigade, the commander of the brigade, Tahir Sinani, lost his life, together with four others, while preparing an explosion material. I was made aware of this after the event happened, when they reported to me the death of these five persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you think that a high-ranking officer, whose troops would possess several thousands of mines and who would not know about it, could be said to be in control of his troops?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that this was at the responsibility of the brigades. I never gave any instructions to procure the brigades with explosive materials. I only give instructions for equipment, for clothing, for weapons, and other quarter master materials.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Isn't the truth, Mr. Ostreni, that you are pulling away, so to say, from the fact that your organisation not only possessed thousands of such items, but also used them, because now is to say that the NLA was an army and the use of illegal means, such as mines, would go contrary to that picture? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I agree with the following: I gave instructions not to use such material, and I never gave instructions for them to be procured with mines and other ordnance, because people who were members of the NLA were not familiar with mines. There were no prepared person who would give such instructions on how to use mines.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can the witness please be shown what is Exhibit 1D260, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Ostreni, this is another article. It comes from another military magazine, from the same publishing house. It's Jane's Defence Weekly, and it is dated 29 August 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if the registry could please scroll down to the second half of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: There is a piece, Mr. Ostreni, called: How many weapons in Macedonia? There is just one item that I would like to bring to your attention. It is on the column on the right-hand side which says: "Estimates of NLA arms holdings." If you scroll down the list of weapons, which Jane's estimated your organisation possessed, the last-but-one item is "land-mine," which they estimated at more than 5.000 land-mines in possession of your organisation, and the footnote suggests that they were both anti-personnel and anti-tank mines. Do you know of any such stocks being held by your organisation, stocks of land-mines, that is?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand English very well. I see that it is an assessment. I know that in the end, when the weapons were handed over, certain explosive devices were handed over, but 5.000 is too much. That would mean that every soldier of the NLA would have been equipped with one, because, as I already explained, together with the logistics, with the doctors, the nurses, we were 5.000. It was impossible for to us secure so many mines when we were lacking ammunition, so that's why it somehow sounds unbelievable to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, setting perhaps aside the number of the estimate, as you indicated, Mr. Ostreni, you were part of the Operation Essential Harvest at the end of the crisis; and, during that operation, your organisation, the NLA, gave up more than a thousand mines and grenades. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have the records before me. As I said, they probably were handed over, but this was at a brigade level, and I'm very happy to they handed over them. I didn't maintain those records. The records were made by the organs at the brigade level. Maybe there are mines that were connected on other territories as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But when you said: "We did not have anti-tank mines, and I sent my instruction not to use mines because they were prohibited by international law," Mr. Ostreni, you knew that to be false. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not correct. My instructions were for such explosive materials not to be procured. Of course, it is possible that breaches were made, but I'm just telling what I did, what my instructions were.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can the witness please be shown Exhibit P493, please. I see the time, Your Honour. Would that be a convenient time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. We will have the first break now. We resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Ostreni, before we go back to the NATO documents which I wish to show you, I'd like to show you another document first.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: This is Rule 65 ter 778.19. Thank you. I believe there is a Macedonian version for, Mr. Ostreni, at R062-6 -- yes. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Ostreni, do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct that this document is, in fact, a record of the weapons which were collected after the operation called Essential Harvest? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that a document which you gave to the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I got it from NATO.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is it correct that in this document, Mr. Ostreni, under number 6, it records the fact that the NLA after -- or in the course of the Operation Essential Harvest provided NATO with 1045 mines and grenades? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So, in fact, Mr. Ostreni, you were aware that your organisation had possessed quite a number of such items; namely, mines. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my language, we call mine also 60-millimetre, 80-millimetres grenades. So we had all these materials.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Including anti-tank mines, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Maybe also the date when this document was given to the witness would be relevant in order to assess his knowledge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Indeed. I would point out that in our experience, Mr. Mettraux, grenades covers the traditional small hand-held grenades and also the forms of explosives used by mortars of various calibres --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: -- documents after that, Your Honour, for that reason --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: -- and then mines are quite a different --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I think I may assist with the second document, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But simply to pick up on the suggestion of my colleague, Mr. Ostreni, do you recall when you received that particular document from NATO?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the end of the Essential Harvest operation, after the weapons and the ammunition were surrendered by the NLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall that among these weapons and ammunition surrendered by your organisation were a variety of mines? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall it. In the part of the process where I participated, I saw Kalashnikovs, various rifles, anti-aircraft machine-gun, and so on; 82-, 60-millimetre; I saw that there were mines for these kind of weapons and hand-held grenades.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps can I assist you a bit here.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown what is Exhibit P493, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Ostreni, this is a document that was in front of you a moment ago, and it is a package prepared by NATO about information relating to various parts of the NLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'd like the registry to turn please to page R042-0361-03, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: There's a passage, Mr. Ostreni, which is in the last-but-one paragraph of that document, or in that page in any case, which starts with the word, "The NLA," and then I would like to read the last sentence after that document to you. It says this: "Besides the standard small arms, grenades, and mines, the NLA is also thought to possess [indiscernible], 120 mortars, and 75-millimetre recoilless rifles.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Then, if we can turn to a few pages later, it's R042- --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me. If you keep reading this, I will forget. There are no such weapons like 75-millimetres, as you are saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you for that. I'll ask you -- I want to show you the other part, and then I can ask you about the arsenal.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It's the same document, Mr. Ostreni, a few pages down the road. Thank you. And the picture is, unfortunately, not clear at all, but it says this -- the next says this: "A variety of mines and RPGs were handed in. Anti-tank weapons include M-80, RPG-22, MBUST, and RBR-M 79. M-57, RPG-2, RPG-7 were also handed in with vast quantities of ordinance." Were you aware after, or at some stage during 2001, or at least after the Operation Essential Harvest, that a variety of mine and RPGs, such as those which are listed here, were handed by members of your organisation.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I accept the table that I submitted to the Prosecutors after getting it from NATO, which listed the weapons and the ammunition that we handed in. What you are putting to me, it's in English, and I can't have a very proper understanding of them, but I cannot exclude the fact that we had RPG, mortars, ammunitions for them, and so on. Whatever we handed in, we had already grenades.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But also, Mr. Ostreni, you knew at the time not only that your organisation possessed mines, but surely you knew that they were using them to, for instance, blow up convoys. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know that. I cannot rule out the possibility that there were such weapons, but I didn't know that they had it, that they had mines during all the time the war lasted until we handed in the weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, let me show a document perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It is Exhibit 1D230. I apologise, Your Honour, this is Exhibit 1D116, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I apologise to you, Mr. Ostreni. This is a document which we have already seen or which will appear in a second on your screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: This is -- I believe it should be Exhibit 1D16, and this appears to be 1D116. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Ostreni, this is a document that we have already seen together, parts of it in any case, and this is a summary of a report that the author of that document is preparing.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if the registry could scroll down to the bottom of the page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Ostreni, this is the same document which listed what the author says are allegations with regard to alleged human rights violations by the ethnic Albanian armed groups; and under number nine, it says this: "Use of mines. "The ethnic Albanian armed group is the only warring party known to have used mines at all, is using anti-tank mines routinely, and is suspected is also having placed anti-personnel mines." Mr. Ostreni, were you aware of any of that happening within your organisation, the NLA, the use of anti-tank mines -- the routine use of anti-tank mines and also the suspected use of anti- personnel mines? Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that. I know that anti-tank mines, RPG 2, 7, were used. Zoljas were also used against tanks, but it is not true that I gave instructions to them to use mines. I'm not aware of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But you agree now that you knew that such weapons were being used. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not correct. I had no information that they were used, and I don't know even now that they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Isn't the truth, Mr. Ostreni, that until the very end of the crisis, your organisation continued to be condemned for its use of such weapons? You must have become aware of that. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't aware of that. Even now, what are you putting to me is in English, and I'm not familiar with English.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'd like to show you another document then.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It is Exhibit 1D15, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Ostreni, this is another document that is a statement by the president of the Security Council of the United Nations, and it relates to the situation in the former Republic of Macedonia. It's dated the 13 August 2001, and, in effect, it greets the signing of the Ohrid Framework Agreement by Macedonian political parties. I would like to read to you...

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: With the help of the registry, if we could scroll down a bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: ... a paragraph in the middle of the document that starts with the word, "The council calls again." What the president the Security Council said at the time is this: "It reiterates its call to all who have contact with the extremist groups to make clear to them that they have no support from any quarter in the international community. "The council condemns the ongoing violence by extremists and calls on all parties to respect the cease-fire. The crowns rejects any attempt to use violence, including the use of land-mine, to undermine the framework agreement, which has been negotiated by the democratically elected political leadership of the former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia." Mr. Ostreni, were you aware of this call made by the Security Council to its president, to your organisation in particular, to stop violence and also the rejection by the Security Council of the use of land-mines? Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which date is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It's the 13, 1-3, of August, Mr. Ostreni. This is a document that was issued after the signing at midday, we believe, of the Ohrid Framework Agreement.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honour, just briefly, I believe that the text reads, "rejects any attempt to use violence."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I continue? At this time, beginning from 5th of July onwards, until the Ohrid Framework Agreement was signed, there were constant provocations by the government forces; and in my impression, the tendency was to prevent us from reaching to the phase of the Ohrid Agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful for that --

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time of the cease-fire, the government forces were reorganised; and contrary to point 7, letter V of the agreement on the cease-fire, they redeployed their forces and brought up Brigade 8, from Veles, to Radusa, Zeden, and so on. And then on the 5th of August, through the media, an order was published by the supreme commander, namely, the head of the state, whereby an operation was ordered to be carried out in Tetovo along the road Tetovo-Zids [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Mr. Ostreni, my question was at this stage --

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: -- Mr. Ostreni, the question at this stage was limited to the statement made by the president of the Security Council on the 30 -- 13th, I apologise, of August of 2001. It was a call to all those who have contact with extremist groups to make clear to them that they have no support from any quarter of the international community, a condemnation of ongoing violence by extremists, and also a rejection of any attempt to use violence, including the use of land-mines. My question is whether you were aware at that time of the call made by the Security Council in those terms.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was aware. But the way I understood, it was that the provocations were carried out by the Armed Forces of the Republic of Macedonia, because, at that time, the NLA was content with the signing of the Ohrid Framework Agreement. And after the 13th, but even before that date, it was not interested in causing any turbulence or falling prey to provocations that might hinder the signing of the Ohrid Framework Agreement. So, in light of a number of occurrences, which I wanted to throw light on but you didn't allow me to go on, this is the way we understood that instruction or statement by the head of the Security Council.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But, in fact, what the Security Council was condemning, Mr. Ostreni, was, in particular, related to two recent attacks by your organisation: One in Karpalak which resulted in the death of eight or nine members of the security forces, and one in or near an area called Ljubotenski Bacila. Do you agree that is what the Security Council was referring to there?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know which it is referring to. It's not in Albanian for me to read it, so I cannot answer to the question you are putting to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But what you know for a fact - and you've tried to disassociated yourself from the attack in Karpalak by saying that it had been carried out without consulting with you - but you know for a fact that members of your organisation carried out the attack in Karpalak with a view to exercise revenge for the killing of one of your members, Mr. Teli, in Skopje. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it is it not correct. We didn't organise our actions as acts of revenge. Our goal was to reach to the phase of the Ohrid Agreement, and nothing more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But, in fact, you knew exactly what was going on in the time in the area of Matejce, Ljuboten, and Ljubotenski Bacila, because you were in phone contact at the time with Mr. Bushi. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in phone contact with Mr. Bushi. He was in Nikustak. That is where his command was based, and I don't have any other information.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I'd like to read to you, perhaps to help refresh your memory, what you told the Prosecution in that regard, and that relates in particular, Mr. Ostreni, to the 12th of August of 2001. You are recorded as saying the following: "On 12 August 2001, I had a conversation with Nazim Bushi to see what he could do with regard to Ljuboten events, but I ordered him not to pass the line that we gave to NATO as the line of the cease-fire. "I told Bushi that the villagers of Ljuboten should be sheltered in their basements. I also told Bushi that he had a right to act against the Macedonian security forces only if they crossed the cease-fire line. I think that Bushi took some actions, but I do not think that Bushi passed the cease-fire line." Do you recall saying that to the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is it correct that you knew and understood at that time that your communication between members of your organisation were or might be intercepted by the Macedonian authorises? Were you aware of that fact?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't aware that I was being intercepted.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: In any case, when you told Mr. Bushi that you thought that villagers should remain sheltered, you knew and understood that he would be capable of transmitting this information into the village. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was on that side. I was very far away, and it was normal for me to give an instruction, if he had any links with the villagers, to tell them to take shelter to prevent them from becoming killed during the exchange of -- during what was going on in the village at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But the reason you were confident that Mr. Bushi would be able to pass on your suggestion is because you knew you had members of your organisation in the village at the time. Is that correct, Mr. Ostreni?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is not correct. I didn't have any information that there were NLA members there. He informed me that the village is being shelled and that the villagers are in danger. I gave this instruction. I told him, "Tell them, if I can, to find shelter in the basements," because the main concern for me was for him -- to tell him not cross the cease-fire line because one day after we had to sign the Ohrid Agreement. Therefore, we had to protect ourselves from any provocation that might be incurred.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, one thing you told Mr. Bushi as well, in addition to suggesting that civilians should stay in the basement, is you told him at that time the fighters, the members of the NLA, should go out and resist the Macedonian authorities. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told him, "Do what you can with your brigade without crossing the cease -- cease-fire line that I had informed NATO of."

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can the witness please be shown what is Rule 65 ter 808, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Ostreni, did you become aware of the fact that the transcript or record of your conversation with Mr. Bushi on that day were published in the newspaper in Macedonian? Did you become aware of that fact?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have seen this newspaper.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I can draw your attention to a section early on in the text, it records the following. At 8.20, it says: "Fazli Veliu told Gzim Ostreni that Ljuboten village was being shelled with all weapons available. Ostreni repeated to Veliu that villagers should stay in the cellars and that ONA members should come out and return fire." Do you recall reading that in that article?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I read there article a long time ago. I don't remember that was published in it, but what I know is there were attempts to systemize the conversations with respect to the events in Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you understood also that this information, which was reprinted in the newspaper, would have come from a source within the Macedonian authorities. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They themselves said that they were the authority who published this article.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, can the witness please be shown what is Exhibit 1D, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Ostreni, this is a document which comes from the administration for security and counter-intelligence within the Ministry of Interior, the UBK, or sometimes known as the DBK, and it's entitled, "Assessment of the high level of the violated security situation in the village of Ljuboten and the surroundings." It is dated the 14th of August of 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If the registry could turn to the third page, please, that is 1D00-5401.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: In this document, Mr. Ostreni, there's -- at the fourth paragraph, it starts with the word, "On 12 August 2001," and I will read the passage to you. It says this: "On 12 August 2001, with regard to the situation in Ljuboten village, Gzim Ostreni informed Fazli Veliu that the villagers should stay in the basements and 'NLA members should go out and respond to the Macedonian security forces.'" Is it correct, Mr. Ostreni, that this is, in fact, the instructions, as you called them, that you gave both do Mr. Veliu and to Mr. Bushi on the 12th of August of 2001?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will repeat myself again. I spoke with the person who was competent person for me, Mr. Bushi.
