What I spoke with him can be summarized in the following: The villagers shall be informed to shelter themselves from the fire coming from the police and the army, because I was surprised by that attack, and that he himself should do what he can, but without crossing the cease-fire line that we provided the NATO with. This is the official document of the organ that was our enemy at the time, and it can be the way they have put it down.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But isn't the truth, Mr. Ostreni, that at the time you knew that you had several members of your organisation inside the village, and that you instructed other members of your group to ask those persons to go out and respond to the Macedonian security forces? Is this correct what you did?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not true. It is not true that I knew that there were this. I don't know to this date. What I think is that there weren't any there, because those that belonged to the brigade should have been with the brigade, the 113 or 114, that was above there. As for Ljuboten as a toponym, as a village, as a location, I became aware of that when the attack was launched on this village. There were other villages, and there was no reason for me to separate Ljuboten from those other villages. As far as I know, I didn't give instructions to anyone to enter that village, and I don't know that there were any NLA members there.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you recall, Mr. Ostreni, indicating that there were a number of areas in the country where you say you had members of your organisation that were, if you want, unactivated or ready to be activated but had not yet been including in your home town of Debar? Do you remember making those markings, three markings on the map?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And if there were any positions in this part, I would have marked them as well. I marked the locations where the forces were at a state of readiness, not mobilised, but who were following the situation closely. But since the cease-fire agreement was in force since 6 July, there was no reason for these forces to be activated for many reasons. First of all, we were waiting for the agreement to continue with the cease-fire, then for political agreement to be signed; and, secondly, if you apply new forces, you need to feed them. You need to equip them with the necessary equipment, and our capacities at that time were sort of limited.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Isn't it correct, Mr. Ostreni, that you had similar sleeping cells in the villages in the area of Skopje?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're speaking of many square kilometres. I cannot answer to a question like this. There are plane villages in the area of Skopje. The area of Skopje is a large area. It consists of 600 or 700.000 inhabitants.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Perhaps I will ask you this, then: Are you aware of any village in the immediate surroundings of Skopje where the NLA was present though not activated, as was the case in the three locations which you marked on the map?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Only those that I marked were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can the witness please be shown Rule 65 ter 1D1044, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Ostreni, unfortunately, this is, again, a document in English only. This is a document that was provided to us by an embassy here. It is dated the 27th of June of 2001, and it talks of your organisation, the NLA, and I will come back to the document on a couple of occasions. But at this stage, I would like you to focus on point C of that document, and it says the following: "The Skopje operational zone includes Skopje's immediate surroundings. NLA groups hide out in predominantly Albanian villages surrounding Skopje." So, in view of your evidence, Mr. Ostreni, you would suggest that this is an inaccurate or misinformed analysis of the situation. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what this means. We were supported by all Albanian citizens; and in my task that I gave to Mr. Bushi earlier, in filling in his brigade, as it was going to be used on the road to Vejce, to have soldiers on the part from Kashiaga [phoen], Zelenikova, and so on. We did not work on creating cells. The NLA did not have any party the. It was a patriotic organisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So, in answer to my question, your evidence is that this document is wrong and that NLA groups did not, in fact, hide out in predominantly Albanian villages surrounding Skopje. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I'm saying is that they did not go there to erect positions, to get organised. We all -- at all times, we acted openly. I will repeat it again. I'm handicapped here. I don't understand English. You're just reading item C to me; and just based on this item, I cannot understand the entire document. Just supposing that you are aware of the entire document, I cannot give my assessment whether it is a proper assessment presented in this document or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps putting aside the document for a minute, I'll ask you a more general question. Are you aware of any NLA groups or members of the NLA hiding out in predominantly Albanian villages in the area surrounding Skopje?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It wasn't necessary. They had their own brigades. They had their own positions. We didn't need people to go in hiding. We needed people who acted openly, who would go openly to their position, and who would enforce the brigade so that the agreement is reached as soon as possible. We didn't need to act in that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Isn't it correct, Mr. Ostreni, that you were actually kept in touch with Mr. Bushi, Nazim Bushi, during the activities of the 12th of August, and that you continued giving him instructions during that operation? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot deny that Bushi was the commander of the newly formed brigade. It was near the area where an attack was being carried out against a village, and it is quite normal that I spoke with Bushi at that time and that I gave him the instructions that I mentioned earlier, to advise the villagers to take shelter, and what was more important, not to cross the cease-fire line.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you recall also telling Mr. Bushi that he should kill the members of the Macedonian security forces if he could?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wasn't necessary. If they entered the territory of Bushi's brigade, it was his own right, because in that case, they would have violated the cease-fire line. And in defending his own brigade, Bushi would have been obliged to open fire. If it wasn't like this, then the security forces would have gone there freely, would have collected the weapons, the war would have ended, and the Harvest operation wouldn't have happened. So this question seems sort of illogical to me. These cease-fire lines were given to NATO. Whoever breaks the line, then the other party should defend itself. So, if the forces had crossed into the territory that was the NLA territory, according to the cease-fire line, then there was need for me to say to Bushi what he should do. He knew that he had to defend himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can the witness please be shown Rule 65 ter 1D808, once again.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Isn't the situation, Mr. Ostreni, that rather than trying to keep to the lines of cease-fire, as you call them, what you and your organisation were trying to trigger is an incident that would make it impossible for the legitimate political parties to sign the agreement in Ohrid that Monday, that these attempts by your organisation took the form of a mine attack in Ljubotenski Bacila in -- on the 10 of August, and also the sending of mortar fire onto Macedonian positions around the village of Ljuboten? Is it correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I have no detailed information or knowledge about this. You are saying at the same time opening of fire, planting of mines.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can the registry please turn to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: This is again, Mr. Ostreni, the press article, the newspaper article, which reflects a number of conversations that allegedly took place during the 12th of August 2001, and I'd like to draw your attention to one that is recorded at 10.54 hours. It's a conversation that is said to have taken place between yourself and Mr. Bushi, and it says the following: "Gzim Ostreni asked Nazim Bushi about how the work was going. Bushi told him that he had moved the units closer and that he was waiting for information in order to make a decision. "Gzim Ostreni told Nazim Bushi that he should have a good decision for any situation and to kill the members of Macedonian security forces if he could. Take the artillery directed on Skopje and 'burn it down'. "Nazim Bushi told Ostreni that he was at position 120 near Skopje, from which he could fire directly at the city and the refinery. Then, Gzim Ostreni suggested Nazim Bushi carry out a counterattack against Macedonian security forces; that is, to respond with a battery against a battery and inform him of that." Do you recall having had that conversation with Mr. Bushi on the morning of the 12th of August of 2001?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recall talking to Bushi, and I already gave you my reply. It is quite illogical what is stated here for Bushi do burn down Skopje. Skopje ask a big city. There was no reason for Bushi to burn down Skopje. If he had the equipment, if he had the capabilities, he would have attacked the forces that were attacking Ljuboten. So that's why I think this is illogical. I gave you my conclusions. I will repeat it again. What I told him was to advise the Ljuboten villagers to take shelter, not to become prey from the attack, to shelter from the forces and the fire, and to undertake what he could regarding this matter but not to cross the cease-fire line. Any other development of what we spoke was along those lines. It is illogical for me to say to Bushi, "Burn down Skopje at 12.00." I apologise, but you force me to use another expression. If Bushi was with the NATO forces, then it would have been possible; but with his units equipped with Kalashnikov, that is impossible. So had I told him anything along those lines, then it would have been, "Burn down those who are attacked Ljuboten." It had nothing to do with Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall giving him that very instruction; namely, to initiate a counter attack against the Macedonian security forces and to notify you? Do you recall telling him that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told him to do whatever he could, because he was there. He could assess the situation. So my instructions were for him to do whatever he could, to protect those villages, but, again, not to cross the cease-fire line, because for us it was very important to reach the signing of the Ohrid Agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can the witness please be shown Exhibit 1D160, again, and if we could please turn to third page of that document. That is page 1D00-5401, and if the registry could focus on the last-but-one paragraph on that page, which starts word, "At the same time."

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Ostreni, there should be a Macedonian version on your side, on the right side of the screen, and I will read that passage to you. It is within this rather chunky paragraph. I think it is it also the last-but-one in your version. It says --

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you just enlarge it a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If you could find -- I believe it would be the last sentence in that last-paragraph-but-one, it starts with the word in English, "On the other hand, Nazim Bushi." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No verbal response]

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It says this: "On the other hand, Nazim Bushi got an information from Gzim Ostreni, to undertake a counterattack against the Macedonian security forces; actually, to respond with a battery to a battery; and then, accordingly, to provide accurate information back to Gzim Ostreni." Do you recall making that suggestion to Mr. Bushi on the 12th of August of 2001, to undertake a counterattack against the Macedonian security forces, to respond with a battery to a battery, and then to report to you? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Ostreni, that what you were trying to do, both in Ljubotenski Bacila and in Ljuboten, was to create incidents that could then be exploited by your organisation for propaganda purposes? Is that correct that's what you were up to?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is not true. It is quite the contrary. You're just putting to me fragments of documents, and you are moving away from what with a was going on in the terrain as of 5th of August. If you analyse the entire activities ongoing at the time, you will see that the provoking side were the government forces, regardless of whether they were acting in coordination or in agreement or not, the police and the army. You are putting to me assessments, documents prepared by the state security service, and we know how they prepare such reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I will show you another type of documents then. I will go back to the issue of your tactics and methods which you used during that period, and I have already gone through the issue of land-mines. Is it correct that you also used other type of explosives, such as thermal battery, which are known as, I think, SA-7B, which are a weapon generally favoured by terrorist organisations? Are you aware of your organisation using those?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first time I hear this word. I never heard it before. I apologise, so I'm not familiar with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I will show you a document.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That's Rule 65 ter 1D868, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: In the question of my colleague, I think that there again several questions. First, he is asking whether this sort of weapon was used; and, then, secondly, he is also implying that this weapon is favoured by terrorist organisation. So I will ask that the two questions be put in one. It should be split, so the witness has a chance to answer both.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: They will be split, naturally, in the document, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Ostreni, this is a document that the Defence of Mr. Boskoski has received from an embassy here in The Hague, and the document is dated the 5th of June of 2001. It relates, obviously, to Macedonia, and the subject of that document is,"Macedonian government has evidence of ethnic Albanian extremists terrorist-type explosive devices." The summary of the document is this, and I will read it out to you where it says --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It's further down the page, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It says: "The Macedonian Ministry of Interior has conducted an investigation on terrorist-type electronic explosive devices discovered in the Tetovo area in late March 2001. The study has not been made public."

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If we could to turn to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It says this: "Argument that these devices found by the Macedonian security forces would give credence to the government's assertion that the Albanian insurgents are 'terrorists.'" The next paragraph says: "The concealment of this study and the evidence it contains of terrorist-type explosive devices is surprising, since it would reinforce the Macedonian government's argument that the Albanian insurgents are terrorists. "Nevertheless, it is yet another indication that the Macedonian government is reluctant to make public the seriousness of the threat from ethnic Albanian extremists. Perhaps it is the fear of worrying the general public or indecisiveness on how to proceed with the information, but it is interesting to note that the government has also not yet informed the Macedonian public of the SA-7B capability of the insurgents." Mr. Ostreni, you have indicated that you don't know the -- or I understand you to say that you don't know the name that SA-7B capability, but were you aware of your organisation using, or at least having in its possession, terrorist-type explosive devices? Is it something that you knew at the time?

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Again Your Honours, Mr. Mettraux is assuming terrorist-type explosive divisions, so he should -- well, first he should ask the witness whether he knows which is a terrorist-type explosive devices, because it --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I have use the terminology of the document, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The document is reporting, at best, second-hand or something worse, and it is speaking of a terrorist-type of explosive. I have difficulty with the notion that something would be specifically for terrorists and not used in general military applications, but you are simply using this document as fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I was trying to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think what you need, as Ms. Regue suggests, is to see if the this witness knows anything of this type of armament, and, secondly, wether it is one of the terrorist type, rather than any other, et cetera; otherwise, we're not getting anywhere with this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I will try to stick to the language used, Your Honour, but I will proceed in that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Ostreni, were you aware of your organisation using any type of explosive devices against targets?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am a military man, and I'm not trained in using such weapons, first. Second, such a letter can be written by anyone, even today. So as this question you're putting to me, what does this letter mean, at the time the security bodies assisted, did everything they could to totally compromise the NLA with claim being that it was a terrorist organisation, that it would be included in the list of such organisations, that it lose the trust and confidence of the population and the international community, and so on. So the answer to your question is that I have no information about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, thank you for that. Do you recall also indicating to the Prosecution during proofing that, as far as could you tell, the NLA did not conduct any guerilla attacks? Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that the NLA never engaged in a guerrilla warfare. I didn't understand the question. Maybe you could repeat it please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes. I will read out the passage from the proofing notes. That may assist you, Mr. Ostreni. It's paragraph 2 of your proofing notes of 2nd November of 2007, and you have been recorded as saying: "We did not conduct any guerilla attacks." Can you recall saying that to the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and that's true. I did say that the NLA did not carry out any such attacks that you are putting to me. My statement speaks about the time that I was familiar with the NLA and when I was there, was a member of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But isn't the fact that it was -- actually the way the organisation had been structured and prepared is precisely to conduct that sort of activities? Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The brigades didn't carry out any such attacks. One battalion of the brigade, as we saw it, had 630 persons. Two battalions comprised quite a large number of people. So you can not hide such large number of people who insisted on the brigades growing up and bringing greater pressure to bear on the government in order for to us come to the signing of the agreement and the meeting of the demands of the NLA expressed in communique number 6 and the memorandum. That was our goal, and that was an inspiration to the NLA to rally around that objective, the volunteers, and to carry out its duties.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Let me show you a document that I showed you a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: This is Rule 65 ter 1D1044, 1D1044.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Ostreni, this is the same document that I've shown to you a moment ago. This is, again, a -- the same document that we received from an embassy here in The Hague. It's dated the 27th of June of 2001, and there's a paragraph that I wish to read to you. It's paragraph 2 of that document towards the end of the page, and it says the following: "NLA infrastructure is designed and best suited for independent guerilla tactics, a loose organisational structure, low interdependency on other NLA groups and commanders. Individual commanders have authority to establish new fighting groups and to evolve fighter structure to meet the military retirement. "NLA brigades have similar structure to UCK structure; NLA fighters are divided into independent operational zones; local commanders have decision making authority; and individual commanders have autonomy in planning of attacks within their operational zones." Do you agree that this -- or would you agree that this corresponds to the way in which the NLA, the National Liberation Army, was structured and organised at least as late as 27th of June, 2007? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is a reflection based on the way the UCK was organised in Kosova, but this is contrary to the organisation of the NLA in Macedonia. In Kosova, it was possible to organise the KLA in -- based on zones, because in Kosova the percentage of the Albanian population is much higher than in Macedonia. If we, in Macedonia, had organised ourselves based on zones or areas, for example, like the Kumanovo, Shkupt, Tetova, Gostivar, Debar, Kercove, Struke areas, then we would be faced with the unpleasant situation, because in this way, we would contribute to a conflict east/west and result in something which we didn't want; that is, a decision or the partition of Macedonia. For this reason, our underlying concept as NLA was not to act on basis of zones as territories, but to act on the basis of brigades that are mobile, can go to this place, so that place can withdraw in case of difficulties, and are not linked with the zones or the areas. So if we were to implement the concept of our military tactic, the brigades would pass, for example, to the eastern area. Still, they wouldn't be linked with the territories. The territories would continue to be governed by local authorities, like in the communes in the north of Lipkov or in our other communes like Sipkovica and others. So, we did not claim to divide or partition Macedonia. We simply intended on making pressure on the government to force it to -- to amend the constitution and meet the demands of the NLA. So, such an assessment as the one you presented here is contrary to the very idea and go of the NLA in the Republic of Macedonia. I need a little more time to make another observation. The democratic distribution of the population of the Republic of Macedonia is such that --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- Albanians live most on the western part, and the Macedonians are mostly living in the eastern part.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... not go into the demographics at the stage, and if we can stay for the time being with the methods and tactics of the organisation of which you are a member. Isn't that correct that the brigade structure, which you've referred to many, many times, was, in fact, just an, to put it that way, an army of paper, and that the real way in which the organisation was functioning was with hit-and-run tactics and, as the previously document showed, with method -- or indicated with methods of guerrilla warfare? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it is simply one assessment. The way the NLA operated, I already explained. It was an army in the process of growing. It had positions which were known to others. It engaged in an active defence, formed new brigades, and pressured, as I said, the government in order to fulfil the demand for which we went into that uprising.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, let's look at Exhibit P493 then.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Ostreni, this is, again the same so-called NATO package, a briefing, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I would like the registry to turn to page 3 of that document. That would be R042-0361-03.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, Mr. Ostreni, that page relates, in particular, to the NLA in the Tetovo area, and in particular to the 112 Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if the registry could enlarge the last paragraph on that page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Ostreni, I think there will be an version for you in the Macedonian language. That will be the last paragraph on that page, and it starts with the words: "The mode of operation for the brigade." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The last or the penultimate paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It should be the last paragraph, and I will read it to you. It says this: "The MO, method of operation, for the brigade is reportedly one of hit-and-run tactics, as seen during a number of successful ambushes conducted by the rebels. These guerrilla and covert cells using clandestine and/or 'terrorist' methods largely favoured by LKCK and AKSH groups are predominantly found within the Tetovo area." Is it correct, Mr. Ostreni, that almost all of your attacks on security forces of the Macedonian authorities were hit-and-run tactics or, as they are called later, clandestine and/or terrorist methods? Is it the two tactics which you were using at the time?

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt again, but I will refer to the second point, which is a broad statement: "later clandestine and terrorist methods." I think that this -- my colleague is taking the words from the document, and I think it is a larger, broad concept.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: A lot of the problem, Mr. Mettraux, is that this document is not evidence. You seem to be putting it to the witness as though its content is the facts. If the witness doesn't accept its content, or unless it becomes part of the evidence in the case during your case or through something else, it is of no evidentiary value. This particular one, though - am I right --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It is admitted Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: -- is in evidence, but on what basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It was a document tendered by the Office of the Prosecutor. It was, I believe, shown to a couple or three witnesses as we recall, But I will put it in such a way, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We move on to the problem that a number of propositions are put in a sentence or a paragraph, and you are putting then that whole paragraph to the witness as though it is the fact. It just has to be broken up into several elements to see what part, if any, the witness can agree with.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'll do so, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Ostreni, focussing, perhaps first of all, on the first sentence that I read to you, and I will read to you again. That may assist you. It says: "The method for operation for the brigade, that would be the 112 Brigade, "is reportedly one of hit-and-run tactics as seen during a number of successful ambushes conducted by the rebels." Do you agree, Mr. Ostreni, with the suggestion that that a hit-and-run tactics was with the one pursued and followed by the 112 Brigade, or not?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not right. But whoever has made the assessment or written the letter is not certain of what he is saying, and he based it on the recounts. He is not claiming that it is so. He is providing information that in Macedonian it says, [Macedonian spoken]. That is on what he heard, or learned from someone else. So I can't take -- accept that. The original document in Macedonian says as I am saying. So the person -- the author is not certain, so I do not accept either the document or whatever you are putting to me. We were always in positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Returning to the second sentence of this paragraph, it says this: "These guerilla and covert cells using clandestine and/or'terrorist' methods largely favoured by the LKCK and AKSH groups are predominantly found within the Tetovo area." Are you aware of any guerilla -- or rather, of any terrorist methods or clandestine methods being used by any members of your organisation in the area of Tetovo?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I don't agree with that. I want, again, to reiterate that the author, who has written this, says according to what he had heard. It is not that he is saying this with certainty. I do not agree with what you are saying about the way we acted, but the document itself also doesn't say so.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you recall also telling the Office of the Prosecutor, and I quote: "As far as I know, the NLA forces did not conduct any terrorist attack." Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And are you aware, however, that a large section of the international community called your organisation -- or rather, its activities as terrorist acts? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't know that it called it such. But I know that, from Resolution 90/20 of the European Commission, the term used with reference to us was Albanian "armed formations or groups," and this is said also by Lord Robertson in an interview given to a group of journalists on the 22nd of May, in which he expresses his personal view, and then he expresses also the view of the institution he represented, saying that: We call these groups "armed units or formations." That is the word he used. So until the international community obtained more precise information on the NLA, its goals and its ambitions, they started gradually to adjust their stand toward it and the terms they used with reference to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Rule 65 ter 1D889.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Ostreni, in the middle of May of 2001, were you aware that the Ministers of Foreign Affairs of the states which are part of the South-East European Cooperation Process, including Macedonia and Albania, for instance, characterise your actions as terrorist acts? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, I am not. I don't know that. They also came to Macedonia, held meetings; and, of course, they wanted to express their support for the territorial integrity and sovereignty of Macedonia, giving priority to the stop of the fighting and the establishment of dialogue.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, the document that is in front of you, Mr. Ostreni, is a joint statement of the Ministers of Foreign Affairs of the South-East European Cooperation Process, and the date of that document is 16 of May 2001. It was adopted in Albania, in Tirana, on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if the registry could turn to the next page, please, and if we could go to the bottom of the page, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: There's a passage that I would wish to read to you, Mr. Ostreni. This is the last paragraph on the page which concerns the situation in Macedonia, and specifically at the time in Tetovo and the Kumanovo areas. This is what the Ministers of Foreign Affairs said: "Ministers expressed their deep concern on recent developments in Tetovo and Kumanovo areas. They strongly condemned the terrorist acts threatening the security and stability of the country, as well as of the region as a whole. "They called on the ethnic Albanian extremist groups to cease such actions, including armed violence, release the hostages, lay down their weapons, and withdraw immediately. They expressed their full support and respect for the sovereignty, territorial integrity, and the indurability of the borders of the ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If we could turn to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: "... of the borders of the country." Then it goes on to say: "They welcomed the establishment of a broad coalition government for national unity. They expressed their full support to its efforts to end the violence in an appropriate manner consistent with the Rule of Law." Mr. Ostreni, are you able to explain why the Foreign Ministers of all the states in the south-eastern part of Europe in and around Macedonia would refer to your actions as terrorist acts and to your organisation as ethnic Albanian extremists groups?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which date is this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: This would be the 16, 1-6, of May, 2001. It comes from Albania, Tirana.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot read this document because it is not in Albanian or in Macedonian. This other languages I am familiar with are Albanian, and Serbo-Croatian, and Macedonian.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, is it correct, Mr. Ostreni, that you suggest in your evidence in chief that the view of the international community and the position of the international community towards your organisation changed after the events of Aracinovo, and that, if I understand you properly, the international community came to accept the NLA as a serious negotiating partner? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will say how I said it, and what my idea is. The case of Haracino was a specific case for us, by means of which we might indicate to the international community that the NLA has a hierarchy and chain of responsibilities, and that we can abide by the agreements. We will sign both with the international factor or with the government or the Republic of Macedonia. That was why it was very important for it to proceed well, and this was the first case, I think, of importance for us to have an agreement, in which the international community, through NATO, contacted Mr. Ali Ahmeti to implement an agreement for the withdrawal or forces of Brigade 113 from Haracino. We were very committed to documenting through our concrete actions that we would abide by our words.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But is it correct, however, Mr. Ostreni, that the view and opinion of the international community towards your organisation never changed, not during the operation in Aracinovo and not after you had been evacuated from the village? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are asking me about the international stance. I didn't have any embassies or any representatives at that time to know for sure whether it had changed or not. After the case of Haracino, we have the letter of the late President Trajkovski addressed to NATO, to resolve the crisis in Macedonia through political means. That was a very significant change which foresaw also a law on amnesty for the members of the NLA. This was significant. As to what are you saying, I don't know. I saw the consequences. The consequences were good because they aimed at stopping the war, on the condition that the demands of Albanians - I'm not saying the demands of the NLA because that represented the demands of the people - be fulfilled; but not only the demands of the Albanians, but also the Romas, the Turks, and other minorities, because if we were allowed to use our national flag, for example, the Turk minority or the Roma minority might also use their own respective national flags. I don't know if I gave you an answer to the question you posed to me, but I didn't have the possibility draw a conclusion on the stand of the international media at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux, it is time for our second break. We resume at 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Ostreni, is it correct that rather than improving, the view that the international community took of your organisation, after the events of Aracinovo, in fact, got worse? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not correct. On the contrary, regular contacts began between NATO representatives, namely, Mr. Peter Feith, and us.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can the witness please be shown what is Rule 65 ter 1D438, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Ostreni, this is or this will be a statement of the Russian Foreign Ministry's official spokesman in the situation in Macedonia, and it's dated 26th of June of 2001, one day after the evacuation of the NLA from Aracinovo. This is what the Minister of Foreign Affairs of Russia said: "Tensions in that country are not becoming less intense. It happens for the very same reason: Terrorists continue their destructive activities and certain circles put forward political demands, the realisation of which could lead to actual disintegration of the state." Then, in the next paragraph, it says: "A way out of the current situation needs to be sought by putting an end to terrorist armed action in the first place, the disarmaments of terrorists, and the disbandment of the illegal armed groups, as well as by continuing political dialogue by the lawful elected representatives of the Albanian population." Were you aware, Mr. Ostreni, of this rather strong condemnation of your organisation by the Russian Minister for Foreign Affairs?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But this was the policy of the Russian Minister and probably his state, a permanent stance including other countries that were militarily assisting the Macedonian forces in their warfare against the NLA. We have the Ukranian uniform --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Helicopters, ammunition, and so on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This statement does not surprise me. However, what the minister is stating here, we had first to agree on our political demands, then the issue of handing over weapons, to whom we shall hand over weapons. All this these things were done on our part. These statements, I don't think that they had a good aim as far as the Albanian people in Macedonia were concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But is it correct that two days after you were evacuated from Aracinovo, the president, through his press secretary, who is press secretary of the United States, condemned your activities in terms of terrorist violence? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't aware of that. All the states were at work. The situation was moving towards the signing of the agreement. The conditions to put an end to the war were being created, and the situation was moving towards the signing of the agreement and the demobilisation of the NLA. All this was brought to the signing of the Ohrid Agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, could the witness please be shown what is Rule 65 ter 1D715, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Ostreni, this is a document. It's a statement by the press secretary of the White House or the president of the United States, George W. Bush, and it's dated 27th of June, 2001. I would like to read to you a number of passages of that document, and it first says this. This is the first paragraph of this the document: "The United States has joined with its European alleys and other countries of the United Nations in strongly condemning the terrorist violence perpetrated by armed extremists determined to destabilize the democratic multi-ethnic government of Macedonia. "Their violent tactics threaten US and international efforts to promote regional peace and stability, and pose a potential danger to US military forces and other Americans supporting peacekeeping efforts." So do you agree, Mr. Ostreni, that not only Russia, but at least the United States, was attempting your activities in terms of terrorist violence and suggesting that your tactics, violent tactics, were threatening the US and international efforts to promote peace and stability? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The text uses the word -- or the Republic of Macedonia is defined as a democratic state. I believe that the United States of America were not justly informed by the competent authorities in Macedonia, who told them that real democracy was going on in Macedonia. This was not true. Had such a democracy had been in place, there would not have been any need for clashes or for an Ohrid Framework Agreement. I believe that, at that time, all the information in possession of the United States and other states were that Macedonia, as promoted by the president before the late President Trajkovski, is oasis of peace. If Macedonia was such an oasis, I would have -- we would have condemned such an uprising. That would be an adventure in conditions of full democracy, but the reality shows a situation otherwise. That's why we had the Ohrid Framework Agreement was also promoted by representatives of the United States, and we do thank you them for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: We'll come to the Ohrid Framework Agreement in a minute; but at this stage, let's stick with this document. The president, or the press secretary on behalf of the president, then goes on to say this: "As the president stated in Europe, we must face down extremists in Macedonia and elsewhere who seek to use violence to redraw borders or subvert the democratic process." Is it your evidence, Mr. Ostreni, that the American president, through his secretary, was also misinformed of the fact that you were using violence to redraw borders and subverting the democratic process?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The National Liberation Army never ever wanted to change the borders. It disarmed, it turned into a political party, and everybody were committed, including the Association of War Veterans, towards safeguarding the territorial integrity and sovereignty of the Republic of Macedonia, and for co-existence between all equal citizens. We wanted a state that would guarantee all its citizens equal rights. This was what I wanted to the say, and you can find proof of this at any time. The NLA never wanted the borders to change. On the contrary, it was against the proposal of the academy of science for the partition of the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And are you aware that at the time, Mr. Ostreni, when you said the profile of your organisation was improving, after you pulled out of Aracinovo on the 25th of June, the president of the United States, in fact, took a number of measures against your organisation and yourself personally? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm aware of that. And, at the same time, I would like to extend my gratitude to the president, who have rightfully assessed my activities; and now, as a result, I can still visit the United States and visit my family, my daughter.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, is it correct that in June of 2007 [sic], in particular on the 27th of June of 2001, 2001 - I apologise - you were regarded as an individual who actively obstruct the implementation of, in this case, Security Council Resolution 1244, and who otherwise seek to undermine peace and stability in the region? Was it the basis on which restrictions were placed on you and other colleagues from your organisation?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is true. I was on the so-called black list of the United States of America; but, as I already stated, thanks to the president and the competent organ that assessed positively my activities, I was removed from that list and I'm no longer in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But is it correct that the situation for your organisation over the next few weeks did not exactly improve; and, for instance, are you aware that on the 10th of July 2001, the OSCE Parliamentary Assembly passed a resolution, referring to your actions as "acts of terrorism." Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are aware that a week later, on the 17th of July, the Council of the European Union was referring to you as terrorists and was imposing travel restrictions on members of your organisation, including, I believe, yourself? Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am aware of the fact that I was on the black list of the honoured president, Mr. Bush. Maybe I was on other black lists. But for me, it was important to act pursuant to the moral knowns and laws and to be committed to achieving progress. So they, later on, assessed my activities, and they saw that I was moving towards the right path and removed me from these lists.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But the reality is that the in course of the year 2001, you were never regarded by any party, prior to the Ohrid Framework Agreement, as a valid negotiating partner. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They assessed this issue. I had the political representative superior to me, who was, at the same time, the supreme commander. He was holding political meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But is it correct, for instance, to take an example, Mr. Ostreni, you referred a number of times to a cease-fire -- what you referred to as a cease-fire agreement dated the 5th of July of 2001. But, rather than being agreement, Mr. Ostreni, is that correct that this was, in fact, an unilateral decision, or an unilateral order in the case of the Macedonia army, ceasing firing on that date? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We agreed, too, with NATO and respected that cease-fire as our 6. A fact as a proof to this is that on the 5th, I provided NATO with location of our positions. This proves that we were in contact with NATO. Mr. Ali Ahmeti was in direct contact with that. I was Chief of Staff. I provided for their requests, and all I can say is that that we abided by this cease-fire agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, we will come, in a minute, to the abidance part.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But could the witness please be shown Rule 65 ter 317, please. The Macedonian version would be at N001-4731.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Ostreni, what I am about to show you, in Macedonian as well, is the order by General Petrovski, Pande Petrovski, the Chief of Staff of the army at the time. It's dated the 5th of July, 2001, and I'd like to read to you the first full paragraph of that document. It says this: "Based on the plan and the programme for overcoming the crisis in Republic of Macedonia brought by the president of Republic of Macedonia, as well as the letter for the decree of the government of the Republic of Macedonia for reaching general, unconditional, and permanent cease-fire signed by the Chief of Staff of the army, General Pande Petrovski, and the head of the police department within the Ministry of Interior, General Risto Galevski, and sent to Mr. Feith, NATO representative, for overcoming the crisis in Republic of Macedonia." Then General Petrovski says: "I am ordering," and he is essentially ordering a cease-fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If we can turn to the next page, and go to the top of the page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: He then signs it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we can go to the bottom of the page on the Macedonian version, you will have the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is this correct, Mr. Ostreni, that the cease-fire that was ordered by the Macedonian authority was not a cease-fire that had been negotiated with you or anyone else, but one that was issued unilaterally by the authorities? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The mediator between the NLA and the authorities that you mention was Peter Feith at the time; and on the basis of this, the coordination of work regarding cease-fire was carried out.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But you agree, for one, that the Macedonia authorities never negotiated or dealt with you in relation to that cease-fire. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't have direct negotiations. The negotiations in case of Haracin and in case of this cease-fire were carried out through mediators. In this case, it was NATO in the role of the mediator between us and the security forces of the Macedonian state.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you said, I believe a moment ago, that the NLA respected the cease-fire. Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be what is shown what is Rule 65 ter 1D1042.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, this is another document that was given to us by an embassy here in The Hague, and it's dated the 10th of July of 2001. That's about five days after the cease-fire was declared. The subject is, "Albanian separatism crisis, situation in Tetovo and environs on 5, 6, July, 2001, as cease-fire goes into effect."

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If the registry could please turn to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'd like to read to you the part that starts with the subheading, "Comments," where it says that someone "wonders," we don't the name, "wonders at the motivation of the NLA insurgents for the indiscriminate nature of their pre-cease-fire mortar attacks on Tetovo. "In view of the number of civilian structures hit, the number of civilian casualties, and the attempted interdiction of the highway Jazince, it would seem to be an attempt on the part of the NLA insurgent to claim pre-cease-fire control the entire Tetovo area." First, let me stop here. Were you a aware, Mr. Ostreni, or were you made away by your chain of command in any way, about these activities of pre-cease-fire mortar attacks on Tetovo.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before the cease-fire, you're saying. But can you determine the frame -- time-frame that you're asking me about, because even 2000 falls within in this period prior to cease-fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, the previous page, Mr. Ostreni, says that it's relates to the situation in Tetovo and environs, as it is called, on the 5th and 6th of July, of 2001.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: 5 and 6 of July are dates when we working towards a cease-fire agreement, and you brought up not the cease-fire agreement, but the order by Petrovski addressed to his troops. Our aim at that time was not to carry out attacks. We were fully committed to establishing cease-fire. I don't know how well you are informed, Your Honours. At that time, in the area of Tetovo, there are also paramilitaries operating in the village --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The interpreter didn't catch name of the village.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So from this perspective, to speak in theoretical terms, excluding the situation in the terrain, it seems illogical. On the 5th, I worked the entire day with the NATO general to see how things will work, whether the positions will remain where they were, work on preparing the maps so that Mr. Feith could discuss them with the opposing side, and contribute to signing this cease-fire agreement. The 6th is the first day of the cease-fire, and our mentality does not allow for breaking the Besa. If you promise that you will hold to that cease-fire, you will hold to it. You will not break it the next day.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, what about the pre-cease-fire activities which are mentioned to you, which had the effect of impacting on civilian structures and injuring or killing a number of civilians? Were you aware of that fact on the 5th of -- or 6th of July, 2001?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not. I do not have any facts to prove that the NLA killed civilians on the 5th or prior to that date.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'll just go on reading the document. It say this is: "In addition, increasing concerned with the 'hard-core' and ruthless nature of one or more of the NLA insurgent cells operating to the north and north-west of Tetovo. It is in this area that the ambush and executions of eight security forces personnel took place on 28 April 2001. The attack on the ambulance as part of a relief convoy that took place on 15 May 2001." I'll stop here for a second. We've already discussed the attack of the 28th of April near Vejce. But are aware that an ambulance was attacked on the 15th of May, 2001 in that same general area of Tetovo? Did you become aware of that incident?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 15th of May?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I wasn't aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Then it refers to the cleansing and subsequent looting of all of the villages north of Tetovo. Did you receive any information to suggest that this was happening?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I received information on the action by police and the army in those villages on the 2nd of April, when the 16-year-old young man was killed, and I would kindly direct you to reading what the media has written and what Fakti newspaper wrote on the 5th of April. They say that the army and the police have committed vandal acts in that region and that measures should be taken, but I have no information whether the measures were actually taken. That reports speaks about the very bad conduct of the army and the police, and then a sports centre in Popova Shapka, Kodra e Diellit. It was destroyed by the on forces deployed there. There are documents to that effect. You can see documents on the material damage caused to that centre. Therefore, I want to say that it was not the NLA that looted, because it couldn't loot its own people, the people who fed it, who sheltered it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then the document refers to an incident which we already discussed. It says: "The shooting to death of the Macedonian villager who refused to leave his home in Brezno. (The NLA insurgents who were present in Brezno when the villager was shot were all wearing balaclavas.)" You indicated, I believe, already that you were not aware of this incident. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not aware of that. If that occurred, I didn't know of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then the document goes on to say: "And, finally, the indiscriminate bombardment of Tetovo speculates that Ali Ahmeti may not be firmly in control of this renegade cell or cells, and continued cease-fire violations from this group can be expected." Were you aware at the time, in the early days of July 2001, of any factions or group within your organisation that were out of control of Mr. Ahmeti?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't have any such information. I only know that government forces at that time brought the 8th Brigade, who were preparing and stationed the artillery means, were preparing for further actions. I think that now we should refer to what the late Pande Petrovski says in his book, that the paramilitaries at the police forces insisted on committing provocations, and then inviting the army to support them in an unlawful way. This is explicitly written by Pande Petrovski himself, who at the time was Chief of General Staff of the army of Macedonia. For you to understand this better, if Their Honours like it, you may refer to the document on the resignation of the late Pande Petrovski from his position as Chief of the General Staff of the Macedonian army on the 9th of August. He recounts the reasons for his resignation there.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful for that Mr. Ostreni, and I'll ask you another question about the other agreement to which you've referred on a number of occasion, the Ohrid Framework Agreement. Is that correct that the democratically-elected parties of Macedonia, whether representing the interests of ethnic Albanians, ethnic Macedonians, or both, refused to negotiate that agreement with you and actually considered the agreement a way to isolate you? Are you aware of that fact?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true that the side representing the political parties and the Macedonian government aimed at isolating the NLA and preventing it from participating in the talks on the preparation of the Ohrid Agreement. But as we said earlier, there was a previous agreement signed between the political leader of the NLA and the political -- Albanian political parties, the agreement that foresaw all the demands of the NLA, because the political parties were of the same mind, that these demands represented the wishes and demands of the entire Albanian population. After this agreement, there was a number of agreement that started to be made, describing the political leaders as bad persons for having negotiated and signed agreement with the NLA, but this did not prevent them from continuing their work and to prepare the agreement. I can say that they were in contact -- contacts -- in continuous contact with the political leaders of the NLA. The NLA did not insist that it participate in negotiations, by all means, because for that, for the NLA it was important that negotiations start and that they come to the phase of signing a political agreement, including the demands of the NLA, put an end to the war and realise the objective of the Albanian people in the Republic of Macedonia in 2001. For this reason, it is very normal that part that in the body that worked for preparing and coming to this political agreement, Ohrid Agreement, where the political parties forming the broad coalition government, along with political leaders who constantly consulted Ali Ahmeti, the political representative of the NLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But, in fact, Mr. Ostreni, far from being a document that reflects your interests and the interests of your organisation, the instrument, the Ohrid Framework Agreement that was adopted by the competent and democratically elected party, was a direct and specific rejection of your actions and the very existence of your group. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not correct. It was a wartime. The situation was tense. All feared and an interethnic war. For the sake of -- for the sake of the vanity of someone to take part in that, it was not proper that we insist on being member in the round table where this issue would be discussed, because by so doing we would continue the situation of chaos and uncertainty. Therefore, for us, it was sufficient to have the Prizren agreement and what we had done so far, in order for the objectives of the NLA to be realised. This is how we saw it, and this is how we worked.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, let me show you two documents, Mr. Ostreni.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The first one is Rule 65 ter 1D705. It's 1D00-6237.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Ostreni, this is a -- the record of a meeting at the general assembly of the United Nations on the 12th of November of 2001, and there's a number of people and representatives of their states that made a statement before the General Assembly. The one I would like to show is the one by the Foreign Minister of the Republic of Macedonia on that occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That would be further down on that page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: First, there is a summary, and I will go back, afterwards, to the more specific statement. The Foreign Minister said this, and it says: "The Foreign Minister of the former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia said that eight months ago, her country had been exposed to violent terrorist attacks under the cloak of a struggle for minority and human rights by the so-called National Liberation Army, which sought to realise one aim: The division of Macedonia and the changing of the region's borders."

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then if we turn to page 1D00-6245. The actual record would be at the bottom of the page, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The actual record of what the Minister of Foreign Affairs said, Ms. Ilinka Mitreva, is being given. We can see at the bottom of the page the start of her statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we can turn to the next page, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: There's a paragraph starting with the word: "For the past ten years." This is what she told the General Assembly: "For the past ten years, the former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia, a factor for stability in the Balkans, has developed a democratic society. Our interethnic relations were held up as an example and applauded by the region. "Then, eight months ago, Macedonia was exposed to violent terrorist attacks threatening to undermine all our achievements. Under the cloak of the struggle for minority and human rights, the so-called National Liberation Army, whose structure, command, control, and logistics of Kosovo provenance, set out to realise one aim: The division of Macedonia and the changing of the region's borders." And then in the next paragraph, she says this: "Our response to these attacks was military, political, and diplomatic. The framework agreement of the 13 August of this year, signed by the leaders of the four main political parties, is as a result of our strong commitment to finding a political solution to the crisis as the best way to defend our country and undermine the goals of the terrorists. "But let me reiterate that we will also defend our country by other means, if necessary. The cost of terrorism for Macedonia has been high, loss of lives, destroyed homes, thousands of refugees, and internally displaced persons." Do you agree, Mr. Ostreni, that what the represent of the then multi-ethnic government of Republic of Macedonia was saying, still in November 2001, is that the Ohrid Framework Agreement had been aimed at undermining the goals of your organisation and not as a way to give reality to them? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot agree with that, because, first, six years have passed in that time, and the agreement is still being implemented, also because Macedonia was not partitioned, and also because has Macedonia been a democratic country, the war wouldn't have taken place. Not only we as NLA, but all the world, believes that things can be resolved in a democratic way. If a state were about 33 per cent, if we included the Roma and other non-Albanian and non-Macedonian citizens, so if a state leaves out 33 per cent of its population from the constitution and does not describe this percentage as a constituent element of the constitution, if it deprives the large part of that percentage from the right to education, doesn't have its language an official language, bans the use of its national symbols, and incriminates them, as the case was in Gostivar, for raising the Albanian flag, then the lady here doesn't speak really about the real situation in Macedonia. This lady is still in coalition with the Democratic Union for Integration. The party that followed the NLA saw so that this very lady is in coalition with this other party that I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you agree, Mr. Ostreni, that this was not just the view of the Macedonian government at that time; but contrary to what you claim, the Ohrid Framework Agreement was not agreement to put an end to what you would wish to believe was an armed conflict but was, in fact, a way to avert one? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: GZIM OSTRENI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not agree with that. This was something used to put an end to the war and to build a democratic Macedonia. The reason for -- the Ohrid Agreement resulted in the amendment of the constitution, which stipulates some freedoms and rights for the Albanian population, but this does not apply only to the Albanian population but to the other minorities living in the Republic of Macedonia, like the Roma, the Turks, and others who make up all the together about 33 per cent of the overall population of Macedonia. That was a good solution that had it been implemented, a democratic state will be built and no internal strifes and clashes will ensue.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I see the time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. We adjourn and we continue tomorrow at 9.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 13th day of November, 2007, at 9.00 a.m. 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.47 p.m.,
